headline: One Switch Could Freeze All Payments You Make, RBI Proposes
title: RBI draft amendment directions 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions' (23 Nov 2026): mandatory Stop Switch to disable all customer-initiated outward debits; optional Trusted Person Mechanism (1-hour approval above a customer-set threshold; UPI, merchant and recurring payments excluded); digital channels off by default for new accounts; comments by 14 Dec 2026; in force 1 July 2027 (earlier at a bank's option).

sources.outlet: RBI (draft Commercial Banks - Responsible Business Conduct Fifth Amendment Directions, 2026)

facts.fact: RBI issued draft amendment directions on 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions' on 23 Nov 2026

Banks must offer a Stop Switch that immediately disables all customer-initiated outward future debits; with it on, no customer-initiated debits, new payment mandates, new standing instructions or UPI registration on new third-party apps
Stop Switch does not affect incoming credits, ongoing recurring mandates/standing instructions, liens or bank-initiated debits such as loan instalments and charges
Controls and the Stop Switch available through points of customer interface such as branches, ATMs, internet banking, mobile banking, IVR

Trusted Person Mechanism: voluntary; an adult (18+) registered by the customer approves transfers above a customer-set threshold within one hour; no response or a rejection cancels the transfer; trusted person gets no account rights, can't see balances, no liability
Trusted Person check excludes UPI payments, merchant payments and recurring payments (standing instructions, e-mandates, NACH)
All digital payment channels disabled by default at onboarding; enabled only on explicit customer consent
Public comments by 14 Dec 2026, via the Connect 2 Regulate section of RBI's website or by email to mcsdorfeedback@rbi.org.in
In force from 1 July 2027, or earlier if a bank decides (219 days after 24 Nov 2026: idly arithmetic)
Drafts cover commercial, small finance, payments, local area, regional rural, urban and rural co-operative banks
